belief: I can't trust anyone in authority.
origins: Abuse of power, broken promises, scandals, or a harsh parent or boss can teach that people in charge are dangerous or corrupt. We become suspicious, defensive, or rebellious, even toward good leaders.
teaches: Scripture is honest about corrupt rulers, and also about good ones. Peter and the apostles said, “We must obey God rather than men.” Paul writes, “Remind the believers to submit to rulers and authorities… to malign no one, and to be peaceable and gentle,” and Proverbs warns, “The simple man believes every word, but the prudent man watches his steps.” Jesus said, “be as shrewd as snakes and as innocent as doves.” The healthy path is discernment: not blind trust and not blanket distrust. Our deepest trust belongs to God, who is always trustworthy.
self_statements: I have to protect myself from them.
I trust no one in charge.
errors: Believing authorities are either perfect or corrupt.
Feeling betrayed and concluding that all are untrustworthy.
questions: Who hurt my trust in authority, and what happened?
Have I met any authority who was trustworthy?
What does discernment look like instead of blanket distrust?
What does Scripture say about authority?
How could I test trust in small steps?
truth: Some leaders failed me, but not all authorities are dangerous. I can grow in discernment, speak up when needed, and place my deepest trust in God, who is always faithful.
hw_truths: I must obey God above men.
I can be shrewd and innocent.
Not all authorities are the same.
I can give trust in small steps.
log: Each week, note one authority you assessed fairly.
actions: Write who hurt your trust and what happened.
Write any authority who earned your respect.
prayer: Lord, I was hurt by those in charge. Heal my trust, give me discernment, and help me trust You above all, who never fail. Amen.
name_example: Sarah can write: “I can be shrewd and innocent, and trust God above all.”
